commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Expand QDQ contractions over collapsed operands (#25086)

Fixes #25085

The frontend dequantizes both operands per block as `[M, G, L]` and `[N,
G, L]` and collapses them back to `[*, K]` before the matmul. The weight
is also transposed:

```mlir
%a  = iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine ... -> tensor<?x2x32xf32>
%ac = tensor.collapse_shape %a [[0], [1, 2]] : tensor<?x2x32xf32> into tensor<?x64xf32>
%b  = iree_linalg_ext.dequantize_affine ... -> tensor<8x2x32xf32>
%bc = tensor.collapse_shape %b [[0], [1, 2]] : tensor<8x2x32xf32> into tensor<8x64xf32>
%bt = linalg.transpose ins(%bc : tensor<8x64xf32>) ... permutation = [1, 0]
%c  = linalg.matmul ins(%ac, %bt : tensor<?x64xf32>, tensor<64x8xf32>) ...
```

The `collapse_shape` hid the dequantize from the integer rewrite.
`PropagateAffineQuantization` now adds the upstream
`linalg::populateFoldReshapeOpsByExpansionPatterns`, with a control
function that accepts only a `collapse_shape` of a dequantize consumed
by:

- a `linalg.transpose`. The collapse moves after the transpose, and the
existing transpose fusion folds the transpose into the dequantize's
output map.
- a contraction whose inputs are all dequantized, directly or through a
`collapse_shape`. The contraction expands to iterate over `(m, n, g,
l)`. The `expand_shape`s inserted on its other inputs cancel their
`collapse_shape`s, so the contraction reads both dequantizes directly.
The integer rewrite then reduces each block in i32 and sums the blocks
in floating point.

Assisted by: Claude

Signed-off-by: Thomas Ziereis <ziereis@roofline.ai>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
